strings.name: Nawaf Salam
strings.role: Prime minister of Lebanon and former ICJ president
strings.summary: Nawaf Salam is a Lebanese jurist, scholar and diplomat who served as permanent representative to the United Nations before joining the International Court of Justice in 2018 and becoming its president in 2024. Designated to form a government in 2025, he resigned from the Court, formed a cabinet in February and secured parliamentary confidence as Lebanon's prime minister. His career connects international law, multilateral diplomacy and domestic governance. His government faces reconstruction, fiscal reform and restoration of public services; reform pledges and financing arrangements must be assessed separately from implementation.
strings.coverageNote: Sources checked through November 18, 2026. English and Arabic reports confirm his November 16 meeting with a World Bank delegation. The account distinguishes the ICJ from the ICC, scheduled terms from actual departures, designation from cabinet formation and confidence votes, and financing approval from disbursement, construction and completion.
strings.influence.rationale: His move from diplomacy and the International Court of Justice into Lebanon's government leadership has given him public influence in international law and rebuilding national governance.
strings.facts.f1.label: Birth and legal practice
strings.facts.f1.value: Born in Beirut on December 15, 1953, and a Lebanese citizen. His UN-hosted candidate CV identifies him as a Beirut Bar member who practised in Beirut in 1984–1989 and 1992–2007, and in Boston in 1989–1992. His work covered litigation, public and private international law, and international transactions.
strings.facts.f2.label: Interdisciplinary education
strings.facts.f2.value: He earned a history doctorate at the Sorbonne in 1979, a law licence at the Lebanese University in 1984, a Harvard Law School LL.M. in 1991, and a political-science Doctorat d'État at Sciences Po in 1992. The two doctorates, undergraduate-level law qualification and law master's are separate. His 1974 EHESS diplôme is not reclassified as a confirmed bachelor's degree.
strings.highlights.h1.title: University teaching and international-law research
strings.highlights.h1.text: He lectured at the Sorbonne and held visiting research appointments at Harvard. At the American University of Beirut he was associate professor in 2003–2007 and chaired Political Studies and Public Administration in 2005–2007, teaching international relations, international law and diplomacy. Visiting researcher, associate professor and department chair are distinct roles; his Harvard visits do not establish a tenured Harvard professorship.
strings.highlights.h2.title: Discusses reconstruction projects and reforms
strings.highlights.h2.text: On November 16, 2026, he received Anna Bjerde and other World Bank representatives at the Grand Serail. With relevant ministers, he discussed emergency assistance, green agri-food transformation, digitalisation and energy reform, urging faster implementation and regional-connectivity studies. The meeting and statements occurred, but do not establish completed construction, full disbursement or completed reforms.
strings.timeline.t1.title: World Bank approves reconstruction assistance
strings.timeline.t1.text: On June 25 the World Bank announced that its Board had approved US$250 million in financing for Lebanon's LEAP emergency assistance project the previous day. The project envisaged a scalable US$1 billion framework, with strategic guidance from the prime minister's office and execution led by the Public Works and Transport Ministry. Initial approval, the larger framework and actual spending are different figures, not the prime minister's personal income.
strings.timeline.t2.title: Government wins parliamentary confidence
strings.timeline.t2.text: After two days of debate on the ministerial statement, parliament granted Salam's government confidence with 95 votes in favour. This followed cabinet formation and differed from MPs' support for his designation in January. It was not a direct popular election of the prime minister.
strings.timeline.t3.title: Forms a new government
strings.timeline.t3.text: President Joseph Aoun signed the decree forming Salam's 24-member cabinet, including five women. The UN report records this separately from his January 13 designation. The new government's reform and reconstruction objectives do not mean institutional change was already completed.
strings.timeline.t4.title: Resigns from the International Court of Justice
strings.timeline.t4.text: After Aoun designated him to form a government on January 13, his resignation as judge took effect on January 14. UN documentation distinguishes the January 13 resignation letter from the vacancy arising on January 14. His judicial term, originally due to end on February 5, 2027, ended early; he did not continue a long-term dual role as prime minister and ICJ president.
strings.timeline.t5.title: Elected president of the ICJ
strings.timeline.t5.text: While serving as a judge, he was elected to lead the International Court of Justice. His scheduled presidential term must be distinguished from his actual resignation in 2025. Institutional decisions cannot all be presented as judgments he made alone, and his post must not be confused with the presidency of the International Criminal Court.
strings.timeline.t6.title: Begins service as an ICJ judge
strings.timeline.t6.text: He began judicial service in The Hague, with a scheduled nine-year term ending on February 5, 2027. His actual service ended early through resignation in January 2025. Older biographies referring to a nine-year term describe the appointment, not proof that he completed nine years in office.
strings.timeline.t7.title: Becomes permanent representative to the UN
strings.timeline.t7.text: From July 2007 he served as Lebanon's ambassador and permanent representative to the UN in New York, remaining until 2017. During Lebanon's 2010–2011 term as a non-permanent Security Council member, he held its rotating presidency in May 2010 and September 2011. This was not two continuous years as Council president or service as UN Secretary-General.
strings.timeline.t8.title: Participates in electoral-law reform commission
strings.timeline.t8.text: In 2005–2006 he was a member and rapporteur of Lebanon's National Electoral Law Commission, helping prepare a new electoral-law draft, according to his UN-hosted candidate CV. Preparing proposals, parliamentary enactment and conducting elections are separate processes; drafting alone does not establish completed reform.
